This 8-month-old has several days of fussiness and decreased feeding but is overall well-appearing, afebrile, consolable, and hydrated. The focused abdominal findings are most informative: visible abdominal distension, soft but distended on palpation, normal bowel sounds, and tympanitic percussion localized to the left lower quadrant. [THOUGHT]  
This 8-month-old has several days of fussiness and decreased feeding but is overall well-appearing, afebrile, consolable, and hydrated. The focused abdominal findings are most informative: visible abdominal distension, soft but distended on palpation, normal bowel sounds, and tympanitic percussion localized to the left lower quadrant. Tympany in the LLQ suggests gas-filled colon (sigmoid/descending colon) rather than an acute surgical abdomen. The absence of vomiting, bilious emesis, severe pain, fever, systemic toxicity, or abnormal urine testing makes acute intestinal obstruction, intussusception, UTI, or otitis media less likely. Teething and upper respiratory causes are uncertain but would not explain the localized abdominal tympany and distension.

The most parsimonious explanation is fecal retention/functional constipation causing gaseous colonic distension and decreased appetite/fussiness. This is common in this age group and fits the exam: soft, non-peritonitic abdomen with tympany and otherwise normal vitals and exam.

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Constipation with fecal retention (functional constipation)

ANALYSIS: Incorrect. Hirschsprung disease (congenital aganglionosis) is an organic, structural/neuropathic cause of obstruction requiring specific diagnostic tests (contrast enema, rectal suction biopsy showing absence of ganglion cells) and surgical management. Labeling the presentation as functional constipation/fecal retention conflates a distinct physiologic disorder with a different, often neonatal/pathologic condition and would miss the need for definitive evaluation and treatment.

VERDICT: INCORRECT
